title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is part of Grothendieck's 1986 attempt at a point-free axiomatics for tame ('modérée') topology. He works with a 'magnifique structure' (≤, ≪, ≭) on a set M of 'pieces' (closed tame sets or cells). Reading the relations from context:
- ≤ is inclusion.
- ≪ is 'contained in'; ∘≪ is 'contained in the interior of'.
- X̃ is the set of pieces ≤ X.
- L = X̃ ∩ Ỹ is the common sub-configuration of X and Y.
- Omb(·) is the 'ombre' (shadow), the set of points of a piece; Omb(·)° is its interior part.
- X|o|Y means X and Y have disjoint interiors (no overlap).
- X ≭ Y means X and Y meet cleanly, only along L. The next page makes this precise: X ≭ Y iff X1|o|Y1 for all X1 ∈ X̃\L and Y1 ∈ Ỹ\L.
- X∥Y means X ≭ Y and L = ∅ (disjoint). Proposition 1 on the previous page says X∥Y iff X'|o|Y' for all faces X', Y'.

Goal. Proposition 2 (checking axiom AtC): X ≭ Y iff condition C holds. Condition C: for all X' ≪ X and Y' ≪ Y whose traces X'_L = X̃'∩Omb(L) and Y'_L are empty, we have X'∥Y'.

Proof of ⇒ (this page).
1. Take X', Y' with empty L-traces. One must show X''|o|Y'' for all X'' ≤ X' and Y'' ≤ Y'.
2. Since X''_L ⊂ X'_L = ∅, X'' and Y'' satisfy the same hypotheses, so one may assume X'' = X' and Y'' = Y' (OPS).
3. By axiom Mag M3, choose X1, Y1 with X' ∘≪ X1 ≤ X and Y' ∘≪ Y1 ≤ Y.
4. X1 ∉ L, since otherwise X' ∈ L̃ and X'_L ≠ ∅. Likewise Y1 ∉ L.
5. Hence X1|o|Y1 by the hypothesis X ≭ Y.
6. Mag 5'' says |o| is inherited by pieces contained in the interiors. So X'|o|Y'. QED.

Attempt at ⇐ (not finished on this page). Assume C; take X' ∈ X̃\L and Y' ∈ Ỹ\L, and aim to show X'|o|Y'. He passes to points:
1. For x ∈ Omb(X')°, one has x_L = ∅. Otherwise x_L = x, so x ≪ L, so Omb(X')∩Omb(L) = Omb(X'_L) ≠ ∅, contradicting the condition.
2. Similarly y_L = ∅, so C gives x∥y.
3. This leads him to isolate a key Proposition(?): X|o|Y ⇔ x∥y for all x ∈ Omb(X)°, y ∈ Omb(Y)°. That is, interior-disjointness is detected on points.

On the next page he notes that ⇒ follows from Mag 5''. The converse he instead proposes to take as the definition of |o|, under extra axioms L1–L3. With that definition he rewrites X ≭ Y as: points of Omb(X)\Omb(L) and Omb(Y)\Omb(L) are pairwise disjoint.

Purpose. This lets the 'clean intersection' relation and the interior-disjointness relation be recovered from points (shadows). It is a consistency check between his point-free axioms (Mag) and the axioms with points (L1–L3, AtC).
errors: The converse direction is not completed on this page. It is reduced to the pointwise characterization of |o|, whose ⇐ direction Grothendieck does not prove; on p.105 he adopts it as a definition under L1–L3. Proposition 2 thus remains conditional (marked '(?)').

The step 'x_L ≠ ∅ ⇒ x_L = x' tacitly uses that points are atoms (their trace on L is all or nothing). The step 'x ∈ Omb(X')° and x ≪ L ⇒ X'_L ≠ ∅' tacitly uses a cell-complex-like property: the interior of a piece not in L does not meet Omb(L) unless the piece has a face in L. Both presumably come from the L-axioms but are not stated here.
Minor: the argument 'X1 ∈ L ⇒ X' ∈ L̃ ⇒ X'_L ≠ ∅' needs X' to be nonempty (have nonempty shadow).

ideas.what: Characterization of clean/proper intersection X ≭ Y: all shrunk pieces avoiding the common part L are disjoint.
ideas.modern_name: clean intersection / general position of cells or strata in a tame (o-minimal-type) stratified structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in PL/stratification theory; tame topology axiomatics: van den Dries et al. (o-minimality)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) §5 only sketches the wish for a 'topologie modérée'; this axiomatics is unpublished

ideas.what: Point-free relations: interior containment ∘≪, interior-disjointness |o|, disjointness ∥, with stability axiom Mag 5'' (|o| inherited under ∘≪-shrinking) used to derive results.
ideas.modern_name: well-inside / non-tangential proper part relations (de Vries proximity algebras, Region Connection Calculus NTPP/DR/DC)
ideas.usually_credited_to: de Vries (1962); Whitehead, de Laguna, Clarke (1980s); Randell–Cui–Cohn RCC (1992)

ideas.what: Recovering the overlap relation from points: X|o|Y iff all interior points ('ombre intérieure') are pairwise disjoint; proposed as the definition of |o| when point axioms L1–L3 hold.
ideas.modern_name: point-based semantics of a mereotopology (representation of region algebras by point sets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stone/de Vries-type representation theorems; mereotopology literature (Pratt-Hartmann, Düntsch–Winter)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'magnifique structure' (≤, ≪, ∘≪, ≭, |o|, ∥) is an independent region-based (point-free) axiomatization of tame topology. Points are recovered as atoms with 'ombres'. This closely parallels mereotopology / contact algebras / RCC and de Vries well-inside relations, a link apparently never made in the literature on either side.
missed.quote: Proposition (?) Soient X, Y ∈ M. Alors X |o| Y ⟺ ∀x ∈ omb(X)°, y ∈ omb(Y)°, on a x ∥ y.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Comparing his axioms (Mag, L1–L3, AtC) with contact-algebra representation theorems could show whether his program gives a point-free foundation of o-minimal/tame topology. It could also show what is new in his treatment of clean intersection (≭).

missed.claim: The equivalence between the point-free definition of |o| and the pointwise one (⇐ direction) is left open. It is replaced by a definition, so the compatibility of the two axiom systems (Mag M1–M6 vs L1–L3 + AtC) is not established.
missed.quote: ⇒ sûrement toujours vrai, et ⇐ moyennant un axiome supplémentaire genre AtL1 (axiome de divisibilité infinie). Voyons !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is exactly the representation question (when are regions determined by their points) that is central in point-free topology.

deep.surprise_reason: The proof on the page is routine inside his own axiomatics. The interest is the unpublished, little-studied point-free axiomatization of tame topology, whose resemblance to mereotopology / de Vries algebras seems unremarked. No striking finished result is here.
transcription_corrections: 'X ≴ Y' / 'X ⋦ Y' should read 'X ≭ Y' (not-asymp, the clean-intersection relation from the previous page).
'comb(X')°', 'comb(L)' should read 'omb(X')°', 'omb(L)' (Omb = ombre, as on the previous page).
'X' ∈ X̊ \ L, Y' = Ỹ \ L' should read 'X' ∈ X̃ \ L, Y' ∈ Ỹ \ L'.
'contrairement à X'_L ≠ ∅' reads rather 'contrairement à X'_L = ∅ (condition)'; the line ends with 'X'_L ≠ ∅' in the sense of the contradiction.
Line 'On a X1 ∉ L. (sinon on aurait X' ∈ L̃ et X'_L ≠ ∅)', with L̃ rather than L̊.
The left margin note is roughly: 'i.e. La condition C signifie que ... ∀x ∈ omb(X)°, y ∈ omb(Y)° (?) ... on a x ∥ y, i.e. ... pour x ∈ ..., y ∈ ...'; it is only partly legible.
